title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: The substantial $5 trillion debt ceiling increase enacted in the July 2025 reconciliation bill, lifting the statutory limit to $41.1 trillion, supplies significant headroom relative to current debt levels near $40 trillion. This timing aligns with long-standing congressional patterns of raising or suspending the limit ahead of exhaustion, using extraordinary measures as a bridge when needed. Bipartisan incentives to avoid payment disruptions on Treasury obligations, interest costs, and entitlements have consistently prevailed in prior cycles. While the Bipartisan Policy Center projects the limit could be approached in 2027, the subsequent months-long buffer before any X-date reduces near-term default risk. Persistent fiscal deficits or severe legislative impasse extending into 2028 represent the primary scenarios that could still test this consensus.
